argument_summary: The admissible record supports a narrow certification position, not an unconditional certify-now claim. Aggregate readiness exceeds threshold, rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, and the rollout includes 5% staging, rollback, and monitoring. At the same time, the student aid advising segment remains materially weak and exposed in the initial cohort, and the available risk-acceptance draft is incomplete and not approved. On that record, the defensible certification theory is conditional: certification is supportable only if the launch artifact expressly discloses the student aid advising limitation, with rollout controls treated as mitigation around deployment rather than as a cure for the weakness.
claims_about_business_cost: Business cost should not drive the compliance conclusion. The relevant point is narrower: when aggregate readiness is above threshold and deployment is reversible and monitored, treating this as caveated compliance rather than escalation is proportionate if certification is expressly conditioned on the required disclosure artifact.
claims_about_policy: The policy text is not satisfied by staged rollout, rollback, monitoring, or a small initial percentage when the affected use case remains exposed. It requires either pre-launch disclosure of the material limitation for the named launch use case or approved risk acceptance that actually addresses that exposure. The incomplete unsigned draft does not satisfy the exception. The audited claim should therefore be read as a caveated compliance position: certify with explicit model-card disclosure, not certify on the theory that controls alone remove the disclosure duty.
concessions: The exposed student aid advising segment remains below target and is part of the initial rollout cohort.
The current record does not support any claim that rollout controls alone cure the weakness.
The unsigned and incomplete risk-acceptance draft cannot be relied on as the policy exception.
The present record does not support blanket certification unless the final certification text is explicitly conditioned on pre-launch disclosure.
